what_it_does: This is a high-resolution camera sensor (25 megapixels, 120 frames per second) for professional video cameras and mirrorless cameras. Traditional camera sensors read out rows of pixels sequentially, which causes distortion when filming fast motion or under strobing light. This sensor instead reads all pixels simultaneously (global shutter), eliminating distortion. The key innovation is placing a small analog-to-digital converter (ADC—a chip that turns light levels into numbers) at every single pixel location, rather than having one centralized converter that reads pixels one by one. This pixel-parallel approach maintains high image quality and low noise even at 25 megapixels and 120 fps.
